author: pblizz
body:
## Summary

Three focused commits addressing the documented Convex bandwidth bleed (1.29 GB / 1 GB quota, ~500 MB/day with no real users on the deployment).

- **`perf(convex): collapse users.* scalar reads onto one getCurrent subscription`** — drops `getDisplayCurrency` / `getLocale` / `getTimezone` and migrates the four callsites (`DisplayCurrencySelector`, `LocalePicker`, `TaxLocksPanel`, `TransactionsPage`) to `users.getCurrent` with client-side field projection. Convex de-duplicates subscriptions by `(function, args)`, so all shell-mounted consumers of the users row now share ONE WebSocket subscription instead of N independent ones on the same row.
- **`perf(transactions): default to 50-row page, drop redundant summary mount`** — `TransactionsPage` was unconditionally requesting `limit: 500` AND mounting `holdings.summary` solely to pluck `displayCurrency` (~12 KB/re-fire on a query that re-derives holdings + priceCache + fxRates). Now defaults to the server-side default page size (50) with a "Show all (up to 500)" affordance, and reads `displayCurrency` off the shared `users.getCurrent` subscription.
- **`perf(app): sessionStorage guard on portfolios.ensure to survive HMR remounts`** — `useRef(false)` guard reset on every HMR remount, firing the `ensure` mutation ~700×/day in dev. Replaces with a `sessionStorage` flag keyed on `userId` — survives HMR, clears on tab close, re-fires on user switch in the same tab.

Estimated savings: ~650 MB/cycle.

- [x] `bun run lint` — clean
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — clean

- [ ] Manual smoke: sidebar currency/locale/timezone selectors load, mutate, and stay in sync; tax-locks panel still computes end-of-day in the user's timezone; transactions page renders 50 by default with the "Show all" affordance appearing only when the page is full.

author: mmasztalerczuk
body:
When lowering `v[N]i1 select + mask + sext` patterns (e.g. the canonical `select(cmp_a, gt_lanes, lt_lanes)` masked by another setcc), the OR that implements the BSP-equivalent ends up after DAGCombiner has canonicalized

    (and (trunc x) (trunc y))  ->  (trunc (and x y))

so the post-legalize OR has shape

    (or (trunc (and A B)) (and C (xor (trunc A) -1)))

That shape is not recognized by `tryLowerToBSL` (called early from `LowerVectorOR`, before the canonicalization) nor by the BSP TableGen pattern, so AArch64 emits a redundant `bic + orr + and` sequence instead of a single `BIF/BSL/BIT`.

Fix #197360

## 范围

- 后端：
  - `lib/db/repositories/usage_repo.py`

## 变更

- 统一多币种金额口径：
  - `cost_by_currency` 现在统计所有“已扣费”调用，而不是只统计成功调用
  - 因此 `failed but billed` 的调用会进入金额维度
  - 零费用 / 未扣费记录仍不计入金额维度
- 保持 provider 分组与全局汇总口径一致：
  - 避免“按 provider 汇总的金额”和“全局 cost_by_currency”不一致
- 修正前端空态占位：
  - 空成本展示统一为 `—`
  - 不再把无数据误显示为 `$0.00`
- 修正设置页总览聚合实现：
  - 用 `Object.entries()` 聚合各币种金额
  - 聚合后统一 round 到 4 位小数，避免浮点累计误差
- 修正单条调用金额显示精度：
  - `UsageDrawer` 中单条调用金额改为最多显示 6 位小数
  - 例如 `$0.0006` 不再显示成 `$0.00`
  - 汇总展示仍保持 2 位小数，不改变整体 UI 语义

## 设计取舍

- `cost_by_currency` 表达的是“实际支出”，不是“成功率”
- 所以金额维度按“是否实际扣费”过滤，而不是按“status == success”过滤
- 单条调用与汇总使用不同显示精度：
  - 单条调用强调不要吞掉微小扣费
  - 汇总仍保持 2 位，避免 UI 噪声

## 测试

- `python -m pytest tests/test_usage_repo.py` → `13 passed`

新增/覆盖重点：

- `failed but billed` 调用会进入：
  - 全局 `cost_by_currency`
  - `get_stats_grouped_by_provider()` 的 `cost_by_currency`
- 空成本展示为 `—`
- 单条小额调用支持更高精度显示
- 汇总金额仍保持原有展示语义

## 不在本 PR 处理

- `server/services/cost_estimation.py` 的孤儿 segment / text 漏算问题
- `lib/cost_calculator.py::ARK_IMAGE_COST` 分辨率未分档的问题
- 更大范围的 usage / estimation 语义统一

这轮新增了 review-driven follow-up 修复：

- 单条调用金额显示精度修正

## Summary

**PR 2 of 3** in the violet externalization refactor. This is the behavior change: \`InstallArtifactVersion\` now invokes the \`violet push\` binary instead of building \`Artifact\`/\`ArtifactVersion\` CRs in-process. OLM \`Subscription\` / \`InstallPlan\` / \`CSV\` flows are unchanged.

Commits in this PR:

1. \`refactor: drop hardcoded violet package prefix\` — PR 1 review fix. \`DefaultVioletPackagePrefix\` removed; \`Violet.PackagePrefix\` is now a required field with no default. Empty value surfaces loudly via \`BuildPackageURL\`.
2. \`feat(operatorhub): install ArtifactVersion via violet binary\` — the actual switch. New \`installViaViolet\` orchestrates 8 stages (get Artifact → URL → download → sha256 verify → ensure-clean AV → \`violet push\` → wait AV Present (+ \`spec.tag\` cross-check) → wait PackageManifest). Old \`createArtifactVersion\` kept as dead code with \`Deprecated:\` comment for one release cycle; PR 3 removes it.
3. \`docs: update README and CLAUDE.md for violet onboarding flow\` — config example with new \`operatorConfig.violet\` block + \`expectedSha256\`, new \"violet 依赖与运行环境\" section covering binary dependency / env allowlist / credential env vars / shared-runner argv warning. CLAUDE.md updated to reflect \"violet owns AV writes\" boundary and the new hard constraints.

## Open Questions outcomes (from plan)

| # | Question | Outcome |
|---|----------|---------|
| OQ1 | Does \`violet push\` support \`--password-stdin\` or file-based credentials? | **No.** Verified via \`violet push --help\` — only \`--password string\` and \`--platform-password string\`. Mitigations: \`MaskCommand\` redacts in logs; README documents the \`ps auxe\` risk and bans \`skipPush: false\` on shared CI runners. |
| OQ2 | Does violet name AVs as \`<artifact>.<bundleVersion>\`? | **Reviewer must verify in integration-test before merging.** The code uses the convention; the cross-check on \`spec.tag\` (step 7) converts a naming mismatch into a loud failure rather than a silent stale-AV match. If the convention does not hold we will follow up by switching wait to a label-selector lookup. |
| OQ3 | Does the Tekton task image include \`violet\`? | **Reviewer must verify before merging.** Suggested check: \`kubectl run --rm -it test --image=<task-image> --command -- which violet\`. If absent, either rebuild the base image or inject violet in the task script before running upgrade. |

## What changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| \`pkg/config/config.go\` | Remove \`DefaultVioletPackagePrefix\` const; \`packagePrefix\` is now required. \`Violet.SkipPush\` default-to-true logic preserved. |
| \`pkg/operator/operatorhub/operator.go\` | Add \`Operator.violet\` field populated from \`OperatorConfig.Violet\`. \`UpgradeOperator\` now passes the full \`config.Version\` into \`InstallArtifactVersion\`. |
| \`pkg/operator/operatorhub/artifact_versiong.go\` | \`InstallArtifactVersion\` signature changes to \`(ctx, version config.Version)\`; body delegates to \`installViaViolet\` and returns a clear error when \`Operator.violet\` is nil. \`createArtifactVersion\` marked \`Deprecated:\` and kept as dead code. |
| \`pkg/operator/operatorhub/violet.go\` | Add \`installViaViolet\`, \`downloadToTemp\`, \`deleteArtifactVersionIfExists\`, \`execVioletPush\`, \`validateVioletBin\`, and \`violetEnvAllowlist\`. Imports expand to cover \`net/http\`, \`path/filepath\`, k8s machinery, and \`pkg/exec\`. |
| \`README.md\` | Extend config example with \`operatorConfig.violet\` and \`expectedSha256\`; add §violet 依赖与运行环境 covering binary lookup, env allowlist, credential env vars, shared-runner warning. |
| \`CLAUDE.md\` | Architecture section updated to reflect \"violet owns AV writes / Go retains Get + Delete + waits\"; three new hard constraints added (violet owns AV writes, registry creds via env not config, packagePrefix is required). |

## Testing

- \`go vet ./...\` — clean
- \`go build ./...\` — clean
- \`go test ./pkg/operator/operatorhub/...\` — 22 sub-tests pass (PR 1 table tests still green; \`installViaViolet\` itself is integration-level and intentionally untested in unit scope per project convention)
- Manual \`violet push --help\` check confirms OQ1 outcome

## Integration validation required before merge

- Run a real upgrade in \`integration-test\` cluster (e.g. tektoncd-operator v4.5 → v4.6) and confirm:
  - violet creates an \`ArtifactVersion\` named \`<artifact>.<bundleVersion>\` (OQ2)
  - \`spec.tag\` cross-check does not fire
  - \`/proc/<violet-pid>/environ\` does not expose unrelated CI secrets (env allowlist works)
- Confirm violet is available in the Tekton task image (OQ3)
- Reproduce an AV-residue scenario by pre-creating an AV with the expected name and confirm \`deleteArtifactVersionIfExists\` removes it before \`violet push\`

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- **What to monitor**
  - Logs: upgrade CLI stderr; in particular look for stage-labelled errors (\`violet push:\`, \`wait artifact version present:\`, \`ensure clean AV:\`)
  - Metrics: AV creation latency in cpaas-system, OLM PackageManifest reconcile time
- **Validation checks**
  - \`kubectl -n cpaas-system get artifactversion -w\` during an upgrade run
  - \`kubectl -n cpaas-system describe artifactversion <artifact>.<bundleVersion>\` after upgrade — \`spec.tag\` and the bundleVersion must match
  - \`tail -f /var/log/upgrade-*.log | grep -E '\\[violet|wait artifact|ensure clean\\]'\`
- **Expected healthy signal**
  - One INFO line \`invoking violet\` per version, followed within ~30s by \`waiting for ArtifactVersion to reach Present\`, then \`waiting for package manifest\`, ending in \`artifact version installed via violet\`
- **Failure signal / rollback trigger**
  - Repeated \`violet push:\` errors → \`git revert\` PR 2 (returns to in-process path; \`createArtifactVersion\` is preserved exactly for this)
  - \`spec.tag mismatch\` errors → indicates OQ2 violation; rollback and pursue label-selector fix in a follow-up
- **Validation window & owner**
  - Window: 1 week of upgrade runs in integration-test before merging PR 3
  - Owner: whoever merges PR 2

- Brainstorm: \`docs/brainstorms/2026-05-18-violet-external-binary-brainstorm.md\`
- Plan: \`docs/plans/2026-05-18-refactor-externalize-violet-binary-plan.md\` (§PR 2 row)
- Depends on: #13 (PR 1 — merged)

body:
## Summary

Adds finer-grained request matching plus a reusable named matcher registry so users targeting enterprise-scale suites can write fewer, more precise rules.

- New optional fields on every network rule: `hostname` (`string | RegExp`), `queryParams`, `requestHeaders` (key comparison case-insensitive; named `requestHeaders` to avoid collision with `NetworkFailureConfig.headers` response synthesis), `resourceTypes` (`'fetch' | 'xhr'`).
- New top-level `matchers: Record<string, NamedMatcher>` registry. Rules reference one via `matcher: 'name'`. Strict mutual exclusion: a rule uses EITHER `matcher` alone OR inline matcher fields, never both.
- New `MatcherRegistry` class and `resolveNamedMatchers` resolver. Resolver runs last in `prepareChaosConfig` (after Zod pass 2). XHR header tracking added via patched `setRequestHeader`.
- Builder `.defineMatcher(name, matcher)`.
- New `RuleType: 'matcher'` plus four `ValidationIssueCode` additions: `matcher_not_found`, `matcher_collision`, `matcher_inline_conflict`, `matcher_cycle` (observable today via untyped configs; reserves the error surface for future composition).
- Debug events for matcher-resolved rules carry `detail.matcherName`. `rule-matched` adds `detail.matchedBy: string[]`. `rule-skip-match` adds `detail.skippedAt: string`.
- All four framework adapters re-export the new matcher types.
- New `concepts/matchers.mdx` plus cross-links from presets, profiles, validation, and observability concept pages. README and CHANGELOG entries.

## Summary

Merging a PR while the agent is still mid-turn is unsafe: auto-commit fires *after* the turn ends (see `post-turn.ts`), so a merge clicked now ships an incomplete change and any commits the agent makes next land on a branch with a closed PR — orphaned work. This change gates merge on \`runner.running\` on both ends.

## Changes

- **Server** (\`api-routes-github.ts\`): \`POST /api/sessions/:id/pr/merge\` now returns \`409\` with \`\"Agent turn in progress\"\` when the session's runner has \`running === true\`. The guard runs before the existing CI-not-ready check so a stale client or keyboard shortcut can't bypass it.
- **Client** (\`PrLifecycleCard.tsx\`): \`MergeButton\` reads \`activeRunnerSessions\` from the session store, disables both the main button and the dropdown caret when the agent is running, and shows a tooltip explaining why. Mirrors the existing \`ResolveConflictsButton\` pattern.
- **Test endpoint** (\`index.ts\`): added \`POST /api/_test/runner/:sessionId/running\` (test-mode only) so integration tests can flip the runner's \`running\` flag without driving a full WS turn. Sits alongside the existing \`/api/_test/runner/:sessionId\` GET and \`/api/_test/dispose-runner\` endpoints.
- **Integration tests** (\`pr-merge.test.ts\`): two new tests assert that merge is rejected with 409 while the runner is running, and accepted once the running flag clears.
- **Client tests** (\`PrLifecycleCard.test.tsx\`): two new tests assert the merge button is disabled with the right tooltip while \`activeRunnerSessions\` contains the session, and re-enables when it clears.

author: adsamcik
body:
## Summary

Captures the **unverified same-process coexistence risk** between base LiteRT 2.1.5 (with GPU/NPU delegates) and LiteRT-LM 0.11.0 in the Mindlayer service. Adds:

- A single source of truth at ``docs/LITERT_COEXISTENCE.md`` with the public failure-mode evidence + an 8-step real-device validation checklist.
- A cross-reference from ``.github/instructions/engine.instructions.md`` so anyone editing engine code via Copilot sees the risk in scope.
- Inline ``TODO(verifyOnDevice)`` updates in the two base-LiteRT backend scaffolds (``LiteRtEmbeddingBackend.kt``, ``LiteRtPaddleOcrBackend.kt``) pointing at the doc and the three upstream issues.

## Why now

The Mindlayer service loads **two distinct LiteRT-family runtimes** in one process:

| Component | Runtime | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Gemma chat | ``com.google.ai.edge.litertlm:litertlm-android:0.11.0`` | Production |
| EmbeddingGemma | ``com.google.ai.edge.litert:litert:2.1.5`` (``LiteRtEmbeddingBackend``) | Scaffold, ``TODO(verifyOnDevice)`` |
| PaddleOCR PP-OCRv5 | ``com.google.ai.edge.litert:litert:2.1.5`` (``LiteRtPaddleOcrBackend``) | Scaffold, ``TODO(verifyOnDevice)`` — Phase 1 PR C2 |

No confirmed incompatibility is known, **but public LiteRT/LiteRT-LM issues describe real failure modes** in exactly the places coexistence would surface them. Phase 1 PR C2 added a new base-LiteRT consumer; this PR documents the risk before someone enables real GPU delegates and discovers it the hard way.

## Public failure-mode evidence

| # | Issue | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [LiteRT #5264](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/LiteRT/issues/5264) | Multiple GPU ``CompiledModel`` instances in the same Android process fail when the first remains active. Workaround: close first model, use CPU for one, or restart the process. **Closest analogue to what Mindlayer is doing.** |
| 2 | [LiteRT-LM #2211](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/LiteRT-LM/issues/2211) | GPU samplers ``dlopen`` fail for AAR consumers — unresolved ``LiteRtCreateEnvironment``, attributed to Android classloader linker namespaces and ``libLiteRt.so`` not loaded into the expected namespace. |
| 3 | [LiteRT-LM #2292](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/LiteRT-LM/issues/2292) | ``Backend.GPU()`` initialisation fails on Samsung S24 Ultra (Adreno 750) with OpenCL discovery problems + OpenGL fallback hitting ``CreateSharedMemoryManager is not implemented``. ``libLiteRtQnnAccelerator.so`` not bundled in 0.11.0. |

## Canonical risk note (copy-pasteable)

> **Unverified same-process coexistence risk:** Base LiteRT 2.1.5 using GPU/NPU acceleration and LiteRT-LM 0.11.0 have not yet been validated together in one Android process. No confirmed incompatibility is known, but both stacks may interact through shared LiteRT runtime components, accelerator delegates, native library loading, Android linker namespaces, memory allocation, GPU/NPU resources, thread pools, and symbol/version resolution. Validate before relying on concurrent or sequential same-process execution.

## What is NOT in this PR

- **No code change to enable/disable GPU/NPU acceleration.** The two base-LiteRT backends are still scaffolds with ``TODO(verifyOnDevice)`` markers — they don't actually instantiate native delegates yet, so the risk does not currently affect production runtime behavior.
- **No new tests.** Doc + comment-only changes. The existing build confirms the inline edits don't change compilation behavior.

## Verification

- ``:app:compileDebugKotlin``: succeeds.
- Doc + comment-only changes — no test surface affected.

## When does this PR's content become actionable?

When any of these flip from scaffold to live:

- ``LiteRtEmbeddingBackend.initialize`` / ``embed`` flips to real LiteRT ``Interpreter`` / ``CompiledModel`` calls.
- ``LiteRtPaddleOcrBackend.initialize`` / ``recognise`` flips to real LiteRT calls (currently a follow-up after the ``paddleocr_model`` CI conversion pipeline uploads ``.tflite`` artifacts).
- A new backend joins the process.

At that point: run the **8-step validation checklist** in ``docs/LITERT_COEXISTENCE.md`` on a prototype APK that loads all three runtimes, and capture logcat output for the ``dlopen`` / ``OpenCL`` / ``QNN`` / ``delegate`` / ``LiteRtException`` tokens listed there.

## Rollback

Single-commit revert removes the doc + the cross-references. No runtime impact.

author: brdns
body:
Hello,

Workflow runs in `nextcloud-releases/<app>` repos might fail at the *Download app tarball for signing* step if the GitHub Releases CDN hasn't propagated the new tarball yet at the moment `release:published` is launched. `wget` exits on HTTP 404 by default.

Observed with: `nextcloud/contacts` v8.4.6, job [#25720873320](https://github.com/nextcloud-releases/contacts/actions/runs/25720873320) (failed 2026-05-12 07:48:50 UTC).

```
--2026-05-12 07:48:50--  https://github.com/nextcloud-releases/contacts/releases/download/v8.4.6/contacts-v8.4.6.tar.gz
HTTP request sent, awaiting response... 404 Not Found
##[error]Process completed with exit code 8.
```

The `v8.3.10` release published from the same workflow 67'' earlier and actually succeeded, so the CDN delay is rather short.

## Fix

```diff
-wget "$DOWNLOAD_URL" -O "${APP_NAME}.tar.gz"
+wget --tries=10 --waitretry=15 --retry-on-http-error=404 \
+     "$DOWNLOAD_URL" -O "${APP_NAME}.tar.gz"
```

Prevents the CDN delay from causing another disparity between all future app releases at `nextcloud-releases/<app>` and the [app store](https://apps.nextcloud.com/).

#### e9754ced56054d27c0dbe1fe93286b42ce5b19ec 
Cherry-pick 5d07bda85f02. https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=312712

    REGRESSION: Use-after-free in Node::m_shadowIncludingRoot via destructor cascade not propagating into shadow roots
    https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=312712
    rdar://175103172

    Reviewed by Geoffrey Garen.

    When a document is torn down via Document::removedLastRef through removeDetachedChildrenInContainer,
    the <html> element is removed from the document. Since <html> is still in tree scope at this point,
    notifyChildNodeRemoved is called, which walks the entire subtree - including shadow roots - and sets
    m_shadowIncludingRoot to <html> for all descendants. This is correct at that moment.

    Then <html> is freed when the loop's RefPtr releases it (children don't ref-count their parents -
    m_parentNode is CheckedPtr). This triggers a destructor cascade: ~ContainerNode(<html>) via
    removeDetachedChildrenInContainer(<html>) processes <body>, then ~ContainerNode(<body>) processes
    the <video> element, and so on. Each step calls resetShadowIncludingRoot() on the direct child,
    fixing that node's cache. However, since IsConnected and IsInShadowTree flags were cleared during
    the initial notifyChildNodeRemoved walk, isInTreeScope() returns false, so notifyChildNodeRemoved
    is skipped in this case. This means the shadow root and its descendants are never updated -
    m_shadowIncludingRoot of these nodes still point to the now-freed <html>.

    Nodes kept alive by mechanisms other than JS wrappers - such as HTMLMediaElement which survives as
    an ActiveDOMObject - retain their shadow DOM with dangling m_shadowIncludingRoot pointers. When
    these nodes are subsequently used (e.g., VTT cue display tree updates via an event loop task), the
    stale pointer is dereferenced, causing an use-after-free.

    This PR fixes this use-after-free bug by updating m_shadowIncludingRoot for removed subtrees when
    the root's refCount is greater than 1 (i.e. there is an external reference to the node beyond the
    RefPtr in removeDetachedChildrenInContainer).

    No new tests since existing media tests such as media/track/webvtt-parser-does-not-leak.html would
    hit debug assertions without this fix, and this bug requires a node to be kept alive by C++ code.

## Problem
The data pipeline needs deterministic repository-level split assignment and leakage-safe deduplication before rows can be packed or used for evaluation. Without stable exact and near-duplicate keys, validation/test rows can leak train examples.

## Solution
- Added `SplitPolicy`, `DedupPolicy`, `DedupKeys`, `SplitAssignment`, `SplitDedupReport`, and `SplitDedupResult` contracts.
- Added deterministic split assignment from normalized repo/source identity before tokenization, with fixture overrides and synthetic source-split inheritance.
- Added exact transition, exact before/after, 64-bit state SimHash, and diff-shape hashes.
- Added leakage rejection for validation/test records that exactly or near-match train records.
- Added exact duplicate rejection with machine-readable drop records and aggregate reports.
- Documented split determinism, the near-duplicate Hamming threshold, and split/dedup drop reasons.

## Validation
- `python3 -m unittest tests/data/test_split_dedup.py` passed: 9 tests.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passed: 52 tests.
- `python3 -m pytest tests/data/test_split_dedup.py` passed in a temporary venv: 9 tests.
- `python3 -m pip wheel --no-deps . -w /tmp/codelewm-wheel` built successfully.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Caveats
- This is the in-memory split/dedup contract. Persisted shard manifests and HDF5 packing remain scoped to follow-up issues.

Closes #22

## Summary

- Pick a single active sidebar link per pathname so sibling routes like `/products` and `/products/bodega` no longer both highlight when one is selected.
- Add a `findActiveHref` helper that scans every nav link (top-level and group children) and returns the one whose `href` is the **longest** matching prefix of the current pathname.
- Replace the per-item `pathname === href || pathname.startsWith(href + "/")` checks in the JSX with a single equality check against the computed `activeHref`. `findActiveGroupKey` now also derives from `activeHref` so the parent group opens for the actually-active child.

## Validation

- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [ ] `npm test`
- [ ] `npm run build`
- [ ] `npm audit --audit-level=moderate`
- [ ] Visually confirm: on `/products/bodega`, only **Bodega Products** is highlighted; on `/products` (or any `/products/...` route that doesn't match a deeper sibling), only **Grocery Products** is highlighted.
- [ ] Spot-check other nested groups (Slicing, Production, Sales, Payments, Inventory, Profit) — only one subitem should highlight per route.

## Notes

- "Most specific" is implemented as longest `href` string among matching candidates. This works because nav hrefs are non-overlapping paths and any deeper match has a strictly longer string than its ancestor.
- Behavior change worth reviewing: matching is now **global** across all nav links, not scoped to a section/group. If a top-level item ever shared a prefix with a child elsewhere, the longer one will now win. I didn't find any such case in `navSections`, but reviewer should confirm.

body:
## 배경

Ollama Cloud를 inference-server의 VLM metadata 추론 경로로 선택적으로 사용하기 위한 작업입니다.

기존 PR에서는 `VISION_USE_OLLAMA=1`일 때 Ollama 연동을 타도록 되어 있었지만, 클라이언트가 `POST {OLLAMA_API_URL}/v1/infer`를 호출하고 있었습니다. 실제 Ollama Cloud에서 `https://ollama.com/api/v1/infer` 호출 시 `404 path not found`가 발생해, 현재 endpoint 계약으로는 동작하지 않는 상태였습니다.

Ollama 공식 Vision API는 `/api/chat`에 `messages[].images`로 base64 이미지를 전달하는 방식이므로, inference-server의 Ollama VLM I/O 레이어를 해당 계약에 맞게 수정했습니다.

## 변경 사항

- Ollama VLM 호출 endpoint 변경
  - 기존: `POST {base_url}/v1/infer`
  - 변경: `POST {base_url}/chat`

- Ollama Vision payload 구조 적용
  - `messages[].images`에 base64 JPEG 이미지 전달
  - `format: "json"`
  - `stream: false`
  - `options.temperature: 0`

- Ollama VLM 모델 설정 추가
  - `OLLAMA_VLM_MODEL`
  - 기본값: `gemma3:12b`

- 환경변수 fallback 추가
  - `OLLAMA_API_URL` 없으면 `API_LLM_OLLAMA_BASE_URL` 사용
  - `OLLAMA_API_KEY` 없으면 `API_LLM_OLLAMA_API_KEY` 사용
  - `OLLAMA_TIMEOUT_SEC` 없으면 `API_LLM_OLLAMA_TIMEOUT_SEC` 사용

- Ollama provider metadata 정규화
  - Ollama 경로의 결과는 `providerMetadata.provider = "ollama"`로 표시

- VLM 프롬프트 개선
  - 단순 scene/object metadata뿐 아니라 객체별 위치 관계를 구조화하도록 변경
  - `objects[].positionHint`
  - `objects[].nearbyObjects`
  - `objects[].surface`

- `pipelineOutput.objects`에 객체별 위치 구조 보존

- api-server memory store 보강
  - `pipelineOutput.objects[].position.hint`를 대표 `position_hint` 후보로 활용
  - 객체별 위치/nearby/surface 정보를 검색용 tags 후보로 활용

- 테스트 추가 및 보강
  - Ollama client endpoint/payload 테스트
  - Ollama adapter metadata 정규화 테스트
  - `VISION_USE_OLLAMA=1` 분기 테스트
  - memory store 위치 정보 반영 테스트

## 기대 효과

- `VISION_USE_OLLAMA=1` 설정 시 로컬 Qwen/BLIP 추론 대신 Ollama Cloud 기반 VLM metadata 추론을 사용할 수 있습니다.
- GPU 로컬 서빙 없이 Cloud VLM으로 이미지 metadata를 생성할 수 있어 운영 옵션이 늘어납니다.
- 물건별 위치 관계가 `pipelineOutput.objects`에 구조화되어 저장 전 단계까지 전달됩니다.
- 대표 위치 힌트와 검색 태그 품질이 개선되어, 이후 “물건이 어디에 있는지” 질의에 더 유리한 metadata를 만들 수 있습니다.

## 시스템 영향

- 기본 동작은 변경되지 않습니다.
  - `VISION_USE_OLLAMA` 미설정 또는 `0`이면 기존 로컬 Qwen/BLIP 경로를 유지합니다.

- Ollama 경로는 opt-in입니다.
  - `VISION_USE_OLLAMA=1`일 때만 Ollama Cloud 호출을 수행합니다.

- 외부 네트워크 의존성이 생깁니다.
  - Ollama Cloud API 장애, 지연, rate limit, 비용 영향을 받을 수 있습니다.

- 모델 기본값은 `gemma3:12b`입니다.
  - 지연/비용을 줄이려면 `OLLAMA_VLM_MODEL=gemma3:4b`
  - 품질을 높이려면 `OLLAMA_VLM_MODEL=gemma3:27b` 등을 검토할 수 있습니다.

- api-server memory store는 기존 payload와 호환됩니다.
  - `pipelineOutput.objects[].position`이 없으면 기존 fallback 로직을 사용합니다.

## 테스트

### Unit / Contract Test

  apps/inference-server/tests/test_ollama_client.py \
  apps/inference-server/tests/test_ollama_adapter.py \

## Summary

Fixes #1620. `printing-press dogfood --dir X --spec Y` now prefers the spec archived at `<X>/spec.{json,yaml,yml}` (placed there by `publish package`) over the caller-passed `--spec`. The bundled spec is authoritative for the printed CLI; preferring it eliminates false-negative Path Validity / Auth Protocol regressions on multi-spec manuscripts runs (browser-sniff, crowd-sniff, hand-authored-on-top-of-official) where the caller reaches into the manuscripts dir and picks the upstream spec instead.

Falls through to caller's `--spec` unchanged when no bundled spec exists — no regression for legacy / pre-`publish package` CLI dirs.

## Changes

- `internal/pipeline/dogfood.go`
  - New `resolveDogfoodSpec(dir, callerSpec)` helper picks `<dir>/spec.{json,yaml,yml}` (search order mirrors `findArchivedSpec`) over caller's `--spec`.
  - `RunDogfood` emits two stderr lines matching the proposal exactly:
    - `dogfood: using spec <abs-path> (bundled)` or `(--spec)` whenever a spec is in play.
    - `dogfood: caller --spec=<path> overridden by bundled <abs-path>` when bundled wins over a differing caller path.
  - New `DogfoodReport.SpecSource` field (`"bundled"` / `"caller"` / `""`) so JSON consumers can see the resolution programmatically.
- `internal/pipeline/dogfood_test.go` — 7 new tests:
  - 5 resolver unit tests: bundled-over-caller, no-override-when-caller-equals-bundled, fallthrough-when-no-bundle, empty-when-neither-present, spec.json-preferred-over-spec.yaml.
  - 2 end-to-end `RunDogfood` tests: bundled overrides smaller caller spec (Path Validity 2/2 not 1/2); fallthrough preserved when bundled absent.

## Scope respected (per #1620)

- Did not touch `publish validate`, generator, `publish package`'s bundling step, or polish.
- Polish keeps calling dogfood with whatever spec it found in manuscripts; this fix simply lets dogfood ignore that input when the bundled is present.

body:
## Summary

Slice 2a implementa la chat reale di Aether end-to-end:
- **Backend** — `dispatch.service` orchestra `AIProvider` (Gemini + FakeProvider) e persiste su `data/sessions.json` via `HistoryStore` (JsonStore-backed, sessionId `default`).
- **SSE pipeline** — `POST /api/ai/dispatch` emette `event: text`, `event: done {model, interrupted}`, `event: error {message, retryable}`. AbortController lato server via `res.on('close')` (con guard `!writableEnded` per evitare false-abort in supertest).
- **Hydration / reset** — `GET/DELETE /api/sessions/default` per idratare la chat al boot e ripulirla.
- **Provider** — `GeminiProvider` via `@google/genai`; `FakeProvider` deterministico per test e `AETHER_FAKE_PROVIDER=1`. `AbortSignal` propagato al SDK via `config.abortSignal`.
- **Frontend** — `useChatStore` (Zustand) come single source of truth; `useStreamingDispatch` orchestra fetch+SSE+abort; `useAutoScroll` con threshold 50px; `ChatView` + `MessageList` + `MessageBubble` (markdown live via `react-markdown`, error footer con flag `retryable`, Retry button) + `MessageInput` (Enter/Shift+Enter, toggle Send/Stop).
- **Error model** — `dispatch.service.classifyError` mappa `ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT/429/503/504` → `retryable=true`, `401/403` o messaggi auth → `retryable=false`, default `true`. Il bubble assistente decide se mostrare Retry in base al flag.
- **Wired in App.tsx** — `<ChatView/>` sostituisce il placeholder; history idratata al mount.

## Riferimenti

- Spec: \`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-18-aether-slice-2a-chat-streaming-design.md\`
- Plan: \`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-18-aether-slice-2a-chat-streaming.md\`

## Deviazioni dal plan (intenzionali)

- **\`res.on('close')\` invece di \`req.on('close')\`** in \`dispatch.routes\`: il pattern originale del piano si attivava in supertest non appena il body request finiva di trasmettere, abortendo il dispatcher prima dell'inizio dello stream. Il nuovo pattern (con guard \`!res.writableEnded\`) è canonico Express e funziona sia in supertest sia con client reali.
- **\`useShallow\` su \`messages.map(id)\`** in \`MessageList\`: senza il selettore shallow, Zustand v5 + React 18 triggera "Maximum update depth exceeded" perché lo \`map\` produce un array nuovo ad ogni snapshot.
- **\`config.parsePort()\`** in \`config.ts\`: \`parseInt\` su PORT non numerico avrebbe propagato \`NaN\` a \`app.listen(NaN)\` causando un silent fallback su porta random. Il guard accetta solo interi positivi finiti, fallback su 3000.
- **\`sse.error()\` ora include \`retryable\`** (fix critico dal review): l'interfaccia \`SseEmitter.error(message, retryable?)\` propaga il flag al client. Senza questo fix, gli errori a livello route avrebbero sempre nascosto il Retry button.
- **\`vi.fn(function...)\` invece di \`vi.fn(() => ...)\`** nei test del GeminiProvider: vitest 4.1.6 non supporta \`vi.fn(arrowFn)\` chiamato con \`new\`.

## Numeri

- **30 commit** (TDD red→green→commit per ogni unità)
- **319 test** verdi, **3 Playwright** verdi (uno reale con FakeProvider)
- **Coverage:** statements 96.58%, branches 86.41%, functions 96.69%, lines 98.98%. Tutte le soglie 80% per folder met.
- **53 file** modificati, +2699 / -26 righe.

## Out-of-scope (in slice 2b)

- Multi-sessione con \`SessionsSection\` in Sidebar
- Switcher + edit/delete sessione
- Routes \`GET/POST/DELETE /api/sessions[/:id]\` parametrizzate

## Note dal final review (issue minori, non-blocker)

- \`historyStore.append\` non logga in caso di disk-full (best-effort, accettato per slice 2a)
- \`MessageBubble\` usa \`messages.find(id)\` con O(N) per bubble × N bubble = O(N²) per chunk — accettabile per single-session bounded; rivisitare in 2b
- Retry logic vive in \`ChatView.handleRetry\` invece che nel hook — funzionalmente OK, da spostare nel hook quando 2b avrà più consumer

## Test plan

- [x] Backend unit (dispatch.service, providers, history.store, route handlers via supertest)
- [x] Frontend unit (chat.store, hooks, tutti i component)
- [x] Integration ChatView con MSW (happy path + retry path)
- [x] Playwright smoke con FakeProvider deterministico
- [x] Manual: \`AETHER_FAKE_PROVIDER=1 npm run dev\` → invio "ping" → ricevo "pong" live, Stop sparisce dopo done, refresh idrata
- [ ] Manual con Gemini reale (GEMINI_API_KEY): non verificato in questo PR; smoke E2E con FakeProvider chiude il gap funzionale

## Summary

Two demo-blockers fixed:

**1. LAN sweep stuck at 5% / "Found 0 devices"**

The backend scanner lives inside a Docker bridge network — it can ARP other containers, never the user's TV / phone / printer. Every sweep returned an empty list. The frontend also looked for `items` against a backend body that actually ships `devices`, so even on a host-network deploy it would render zero.

Discovery now runs entirely in the Electron main process:

- `os.networkInterfaces()` to find the right interface (skips Docker/VMware/Hyper-V bridges)
- TCP-SYN ping-sweep of the local /24 (40-way concurrent, 400ms budget per host)
- `arp -a` / `arp -an` parsed for IP↔MAC (Korean-Windows-localized output included)
- Reverse-DNS, vendor lookup against an embedded OUI table, randomized-MAC detection via the locally-administered bit
- Per-host progress events so the bar moves from 12% → 76% as hosts come back instead of freezing at 5%
- SHA-256 `lan_fingerprint` derived from `gateway_mac + subnet`

Results are uploaded to a new `POST /v1/claim/scan/ingest` endpoint so the rest of the claim machinery (ownership challenge → execute) reads the host's real LAN out of the same scanner cache it always has.

**2. Apple / Google buttons no longer log in as "Google Demo · PERSONAL"**

The unpackaged-build OAuth fallback silently posted to `/v1/users/oauth/{provider}/dev-login`, which created a shared `oauth_<provider>@electromesh.dev` user with display name `<Provider> Demo`. That's the identity that was showing up in the rail in the screenshot. Removed. Clicking the buttons now always opens the provider's real authorize URL in a child window; if the backend doesn't have `EM_OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `EM_OAUTH_APPLE_CLIENT_ID` configured the user sees a clear "ask the admin to set it" error instead of being silently logged in.

Buttons restyled to the official Google four-color "G" and Apple HIG black so they read as real sign-in entry points.

## Files

- `electromesh-consumer/src/main/lan-discovery.ts` — new, host-side scanner
- `electromesh-consumer/src/main/lan-scan.ts` — uses it, posts to `/scan/ingest`

- `electromesh-consumer/src/renderer/pages/Login.tsx` — branded SVG glyphs + accessible labels

- `backend/app/api/v1/claim.py` — `POST /v1/claim/scan/ingest` endpoint + Pydantic schema
- `backend/app/services/claim_service.py` — `ingest_scan_results()` seeds scanner cache with client data

## Overview

This PR updates the "Consuming On-Chain Price Data from the Pragma Oracle"
tutorial so it works against Pragma's v14 oracle. Pragma recently redeployed
their Miden oracle for the v14 protocol, which changed both the deployment
addresses and the consumer-facing interface. The earlier v14 tutorial
migration (#186) only updated the SDK API surface, so the tutorial still
pointed at the dead pre-v14 deployment and failed at runtime.

## Changes

- **MASM (`oracle_reader.masm`)** — `get_price` calls `get_median` with the
  v14 FPI ABI: 16 foreign-procedure inputs carrying the BTC/USD faucet pair
  (prefix `1`, suffix `0`), the new `get_median` procedure root, and the new
  oracle account ID.
- **Rust (`oracle_data_query.rs`)** — publishers are discovered from the
  oracle's `pragma::oracle::publishers` storage map (the old value-slot
  heuristic doesn't match the v14 layout), and each publisher's
  `pragma::publisher::entries` proof is requested keyed by the faucet-pair word.
- **Docs (`oracle_tutorial.md`)** — embedded code blocks synced to the runnable
  files; prose, addresses, and example output updated for the v14
  `[is_tracked, median_price, amount]` return layout.

**Closes #200**
**Closes #113**

# ERP Overhaul v1 — Security, Schema, UI, Tax Engine, Payments, Approval Workflows

A comprehensive overhaul of the QuotebotERP platform covering security hardening, data integrity, responsive UI, new business modules, and developer tooling.

## Summary of Changes

### Security Hardening
- **JWT secret**: Removed hardcoded fallback (`|| 'your-secret-key'`) from 4 files; all now use `requireEnv('JWT_SECRET')` which throws on startup if missing
- **Rate limiting**: Global throttle via `@nestjs/throttler` (100 req/min default, 10 req/min on auth endpoints); `@SkipThrottle()` on health checks and webhook controllers
- **Helmet**: HTTP security headers via `helmet()` middleware
- **CSRF protection**: Custom middleware requiring `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` on mutating requests; excludes auth routes, OAuth callbacks, and Swagger paths
- **Credential cleanup**: Removed exposed `testCredentials` object from `/api/docs` endpoint
- **`forceDelete` admin guard**: Hard-delete operations now require `role === 'admin'`, returning 403 for non-admins

### Schema & Data Integrity
- **Float → Decimal**: All monetary fields converted to `Decimal @db.Decimal(12,2)` (prices, costs, totals, amounts); tax percentages to `Decimal(5,2)`
- **String → DateTime**: `Quotation.date`, `valid_until`, `Invoice.date`, `due_date` converted to proper `DateTime` types
- **Soft deletes**: Added `deleted_at DateTime?` + `@@index([deleted_at])` to 8 models (Product, Client, RFQ, RFQItem, Quotation, QuotationItem, Invoice, Payment)
- **Consistent soft-delete filters**: All queries across 10+ services include `deleted_at: null`; `forceDelete()` methods with FK cascade handling
- **Migration file**: `20260518000000_erp_overhaul_v1/migration.sql` covers all schema changes with safe `IF NOT EXISTS` / `DO $$` blocks
- **`sortBy` validation**: All 6 list services validate `sortBy` against field whitelists, defaulting to `created_at`

### Pagination
- Created `PaginationParams` / `PaginatedResult<T>` / `parsePaginationParams()` utility
- All list endpoints return `{ data, meta: { total, page, pageSize, totalPages } }` format
- Frontend `AppContext.tsx` uses `unwrapPaginated()` helper with `?pageSize=1000` for initial loads
- Max pageSize raised to 1000 to support existing page patterns

### SaaS Landing Page & Auth Redesign
- **Landing page**: Professional SaaS design with hero section, 6-card features grid, 3-step how-it-works, 3-tier pricing (Free/₹999/Custom), CTA sections, footer, scroll animations via `useInView` hook
- **Login/Signup**: Split-screen redesign — left branded panel (indigo gradient with feature checklist), right form panel with validation, show/hide password, Google OAuth button

### Responsive UI
- **Sidebar**: Mobile drawer (<768px), tablet collapsed mode (768-1024px), desktop full sidebar
- **Header**: Mobile search row, reduced padding, full-width dropdowns
- **DataTable**: Column sorting, pagination controls, loading skeleton, empty state, horizontal scroll on mobile
- **FormElements**: Error prop (red border + message), required prop (red asterisk)
- **Dashboard**: Responsive grid (`grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4 lg:grid-cols-8`), KPI skeleton loading
- **PromptModal**: Replaced all `window.prompt()` / `window.alert()` calls with proper modal component

### GST Tax Engine (`backend/src/tax/`)
- CRUD for `TaxProfile` model with `name`, `type`, `rate`, `hsn_code`, `is_default`, `is_active`
- `calculateTax()` with CGST/SGST/IGST split based on GSTIN state codes
- `seedDefaults()` creates 5 standard Indian GST profiles (28%, 18%, 12%, 5%, 0%)
- Falls back to `profile_json.gstin` when `company_gstin` is empty; syncs on settings save

### Payment Tracking (`backend/src/payments/`)
- `recordPayment()` with atomic Prisma `$transaction` (invoice read + update inside transaction)
- Overpayment validation: rejects amounts exceeding remaining balance
- `@Min(0.01)` validation on payment amount
- `getReceivablesAging()` returns aging buckets (current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+ days)
- Consistent `payment_status` updates across both payment flows (invoices service + payments service)
- Frontend `Payments.tsx` page with aging cards, paginated table, "Record Payment" modal

### Approval Workflows
- Quotations exceeding `quotation_approval_threshold` (from SettingsCompany) auto-set to `approval_status: 'pending'`
- Applies during both direct creation and RFQ-to-quotation conversion
- `approve()` / `reject()` endpoints with user tracking (`approved_by`, `approved_at`, `rejection_reason`)
- Email sending blocked for pending-approval quotations

### Audit & Observability
- **Structured logging**: `AppLoggerService` with JSON output in production; replaced all `console.log/error/warn` with NestJS `Logger`
- **Global exception filter**: Catches all exceptions, hides stack traces in production
- **Audit Log UI**: `AuditLog.tsx` page with paginated table, filters (entity type, action, date range, entity ID search)
- **Swagger**: API documentation at `/api/swagger` with `@ApiTags()` on all controllers

### Developer Tooling
- `backend/.env.example` with documented environment variables

author: neoplays
body:
## FIX: macOS build

Fixes the unsigned macOS build, which was failing to launch on macOS 14.4+ / macOS 26 due to inconsistent Team IDs between the (pre-signed) Electron Framework and the unsigned main binary, causing dyld to reject the load.

### Background
electron-builder v26 no longer re-signs bundled frameworks when no signing certificate is provided. The Electron Framework ships pre-signed with the Electron project's Apple Team ID, while the main executable has no Team ID — dyld's validation refuses to load the app as a result.

### Changes

**`launcher/afterPackMac.js`** (new file)
- Adds an `afterPack` hook that runs only on `darwin`.
- Ad-hoc re-signs the entire `.app` bundle with `codesign --force --deep --sign -`, so all binaries share a consistent (empty) Team ID and dyld validation passes.

**`launcher/vue.config.js`**
- Introduces `isSigned` flag derived from `CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY !== "false"`.
- Wires up the new `afterPackMac.js` hook only for unsigned builds.
- `hardenedRuntime` is now conditional on `isSigned` — it requires consistent Team IDs across binaries and only makes sense when actually signing.
- `entitlements` / `entitlementsInherit` are likewise only set on signed builds.

### Result
- Signed/notarized builds: behavior unchanged.
- Unsigned local/CI builds: app launches correctly on macOS 14.4+ and macOS 26+.
